mock.pane.title: Mock servers
mock.pane.foot.out: Proxy and callbacks send requests out
mock.header.name: Server name
mock.issue.name: Enter a name
mock.issue.status: Use a status code from 100 to 599
mock.issue.regex: This regular expression is not supported
mock.leave.title: Unapplied changes
mock.leave.body: Changes that could not be saved will be lost.
mock.data.removed.one: Deleted {name}. {count} CRUD route is an HTTP route now
mock.data.removed.other: Deleted {name}. {count} CRUD routes are HTTP routes now
mock.tabs.label: Mock server sections
mock.empty.title: No mock servers yet
mock.empty.body: A mock server answers on 127.0.0.1 with the routes you define. Saving does not start it.
mock.error.list.title: Mock servers could not be loaded
mock.pick.title: Select a mock server
mock.pick.body: Pick a server in the list to edit its routes and see its traffic.
mock.noRoutes.title: This server has no routes
mock.noRoutes.body: Requests to {name} answer 404 until you add a route.
mock.conflict.title: Port {port} is already in use
mock.conflict.body: Another program is listening on 127.0.0.1:{port}, so {name} cannot start.
mock.conflict.bodyOurs: {other} is listening on 127.0.0.1:{port}, so {name} cannot start.
mock.startError.title: {name} did not start
mock.draft.truncated: Only the first 64 KiB of the body was kept.
mock.draft.pick: Add the route to which server?
mock.draft.pickHint: Nothing starts and no request is sent.
mock.stopAll.body: Requests in progress are cut off.
mock.routes.addFromLog.none: No unmatched or forwarded requests in the log yet
mock.route.path.hint: Path parameters are written :id, {alias} works too; a trailing * matches the rest of the path.
mock.editor.label: Route editor
mock.editor.pick: Select a route to edit it
mock.response.none: This route has no responses yet.
mock.response.label: Label
mock.response.never: Never returned: no rules and not the default
mock.response.neverFallback: Never returned: Fall through skips responses without rules
mock.mode.label: Response mode
mock.mode.firstMatch.help: Returns the first response whose rules match, top to bottom; otherwise the default.
mock.mode.sequential.help: Ignores rules; returns each response in turn, then starts over.
mock.mode.random.help: Ignores rules; returns a random response each time.
mock.mode.fallback.help: Returns the first response whose rules match, top to bottom; if nothing matches, passes to later routes, the proxy, or 404.
mock.mode.disableRules.help: Ignores rules; always returns the default response.
mock.body.label: Body
mock.body.validTemplates: {count} templates unrendered, the rest is valid JSON
mock.response.statusCustom: Not a suggested code; any status from 100 to 599 works
mock.stream.limits: Up to 100 events. The whole stream takes at most 60 s; events past that are not sent, and Hang keeps the connection open until then.
mock.stream.limitsDemo: The browser demo does not send streams. Editing works and is saved.
mock.env.title: Environment
mock.env.label: Variables from
mock.env.hint: Variables named in proxy and callback URLs and headers take this environment's plain values when the server starts or is saved. Secret variables are not filled in and go out as written: a secret may only reach a declared host.
mock.tpl.body: A field of the JSON body
mock.tpl.int: A random integer in a range
mock.headers.title: Response headers
mock.headers.hint: Added to every response. A route's header with the same name wins.
mock.rules.title: Rules
mock.rules.off: This mode ignores rules. Switch to By rule order or Fall through.
mock.rule.invert: Rule {n}: match when it does not apply
mock.callbacks.title: Callbacks
mock.callbacks.hint: Fired after this response is served
mock.crud.idKey.hint: The property that identifies one item.
mock.live.title: Live traffic
mock.log.stopped: Start the server to see requests
mock.log.stopped.body: The log shows the newest requests while the server is running.
mock.log.empty.body: While the server runs, requests to {address} appear here.
mock.log.split: Resize the log and its detail
mock.log.released: Not kept (older than the newest rows).
mock.data.hint: JSON buckets are served by {{data 'name'}} and by CRUD routes.
mock.data.empty.title: No data buckets yet
mock.data.empty.body: A bucket is JSON that templates and CRUD routes read.
mock.data.name: Bucket name
mock.data.nameTaken: Another bucket already uses this name.
mock.data.expectObject: Expected an array or an object
mock.data.keepsLast: The server keeps the last valid data.
mock.data.live.stopped: Start the server to see live data
mock.data.live.hint: What the running server holds in memory, changed by CRUD routes. Stopping or restarting the server resets it to the initial data.
mock.data.live.confirmAll.title: Reset every bucket to the initial data?
mock.data.live.confirm.title: Reset bucket {name} to the initial data?
mock.data.live.confirm.body: Records that CRUD routes added, changed or removed since the server started are lost.
mock.data.live.truncated: Showing the first 1 MiB; the rest is not sent.
mock.data.live.omitted: Not shown: the live data of this server is over 4 MiB.
mock.data.live.error: Could not read the live data: {message}
mock.callbacks.tabHint: Outbound requests fired after a response is served. Attach them to a response in the route editor.
mock.callbacks.empty.title: No callbacks yet
mock.callbacks.empty.body: A callback sends an HTTP request after a response is served.
mock.callbacks.name: Name
mock.proxy.hint: Requests that match no enabled route are forwarded to a base URL.
mock.proxy.state.off: Off: requests no route matches get 404
mock.proxy.needUrl: Fill in the target base URL first
mock.proxy.confirm.title: Turn on proxy to {host}?
mock.proxy.confirm.body: Unmatched requests go to {url} with all their headers, including Authorization and Cookie.
mock.proxy.redirects: Redirects aren't followed; 3xx is returned as is
mock.proxy.confirm.hops: Adds x-pingdeck-hops so a request is never forwarded back here
mock.proxy.url.hint: A loopback or private address is allowed. Redirects aren't followed; 3xx is returned as is.
mock.proxy.strip.hint: Leave the prefix out of the forwarded path.
mock.proxy.sent: Every request header goes out (minus Host, Content-Length, Connection and other hop-by-hop headers), plus x-pingdeck-hops and the headers below.
mock.settings.name: Name
mock.settings.port.locked: Can't change while running. Stop to edit
mock.settings.prefix.hint: Added in front of every route and copied with the address.
mock.settings.prefix.pending: Prefix changes to {next} after a restart. Still serving {live}.
mock.settings.cors.hint: Answer preflight requests and add CORS headers. Only a loopback Origin is echoed.
mock.scope.title: Who can reach this server
mock.scope.listen: Listens on 127.0.0.1:{port} and [::1]:{port} only. No LAN address: phones and other computers can't reach it.
mock.scope.host: A request whose Host is not this computer gets 403, including Docker's host.docker.internal and the Android emulator's 10.0.2.2, unless the name is in Extra allowed hosts below. In the emulator you can also run adb reverse tcp:{port} tcp:{port}, then call 127.0.0.1:{port}.
mock.scope.origin: Write requests from other websites (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE with a non-local Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site) get 403: no data bucket writes, no callbacks, no proxying. They appear in traffic.
mock.scope.out: Only two things send requests out: the proxy and callbacks.
mock.because.default: No rule matched, so the default response answered
mock.because.first: No rule matched and there is no default, so the first response answered
mock.because.disabled_rules: Rules are off, so the default response answered
mock.log.openPartial: The request body was cut at 64 KiB, so the draft carries only the partial body.
mock.confirm.stop.title: Stop the server and discard data bucket changes?
mock.confirm.stop.body.one: Changes to {count} data bucket will be discarded. The next start begins from the initial data.
mock.confirm.stop.body.other: Changes to {count} data buckets will be discarded. The next start begins from the initial data.
mock.toast.reset: Reset {name}: sequence and request number cleared, data buckets untouched
mock.settings.reset.hint: Clears sequence cursors, request numbers and the hit count. Data buckets and traffic stay.
mock.settings.reset.stopped: The server is not running, so there is no state to reset.
mock.data.resetsLive: Saving resets the live data of this bucket.
mock.try.title: Try it · {route}
mock.try.mayMiss: You can send as is. The result shows which response answered.
mock.try.unapplied: This server has problems to fix. Until then, the saved version answers.
mock.try.startFailed: {name} didn't start. The request wasn't sent
mock.try.pickHint: Pick a response to start from, or send as is.
mock.try.noRules: This response has no rules. The request goes as is.
mock.try.manual: Rule {n} ({pattern}) needs a value you enter.
mock.fault.hang.hint: After the delay the client gets no response; the connection closes after 60 s or when the server stops.
mock.fault.drop.hint: After the delay the connection closes without a single response byte.
mock.source.file.hint: An absolute path, read on every request (up to 1 MiB, no templates).
mock.source.base64.hint: Paste Base64: the decoded bytes are sent as they are, for images and other binary bodies (up to 1 MiB).
mock.tpl.faker: A fake value by Faker.js method name
mock.tpl.nowFormat: The current time in a date-fns format
mock.tpl.repeat: Repeat a block, joined with commas
mock.tpl.each: One block per item of a data bucket or body array
mock.because.prefer: The request's Prefer: code= header asked for this status
mock.record.title: Record
mock.record.hint: While recording, every forwarded response is kept whole (one per method and path, the latest wins) until the server stops. Save them as routes to mock the real API.
mock.record.saveHint: Adds a route for each recorded request no route answers yet.
mock.hosts.title: Extra allowed hosts
mock.hosts.hint: For every mock server: requests whose Host is one of these names get through, such as 10.0.2.2 from the Android emulator or host.docker.internal from Docker Desktop. The servers still listen on this computer only.
mock.hosts.confirm.title: Allow requests addressed to {host}?
mock.hosts.confirm.body: Every mock server will answer requests whose Host header names it.
mock.hosts.confirm.loopback: The servers still listen on 127.0.0.1 and [::1] only; this does not open them to the network.
mock.hosts.confirm.rebinding: Only add names you control: a web page that points a name of its own at this computer could then read mock responses.
